newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Pharma Vision bought Hoechst stake.
newsitem.headline: Pharma Vision bought Hoechst stake.

text.p: Investment fund Pharma Vision, part of the BZ Group securities house, said it had acquired a 0.5 percent stake in German chemical and pharmaceuticals group Hoechst AG.
Peter Sjoestrand, member of the board of Pharma Vision, told a news conference that the stake in Hoechst was acquired in the middle of 1996.
In January Martin Ebner, president of the BZ Group, said Pharma Vision had invested some 200 million Swiss francs in a German company, but he declined to identify the company at that point.
The investment in Hoechst is part of a new strategy of diversifying the portfolios within the BZ's group's trusts.
The investment in Hoechst was financed by liquidating some of Pharma Vision's holdings of Roche Holding AG bearer shares, Ebner said in January.
Pharma Vision is one of the largest stakeholders in Roche and owns 15.6 percent of its bearer shares.
Pharma Vision said today the market value of its stake in Roche was 5.2 billion by the end of 1996, but since then the value had risen to 6.4 billion.
By mid-1996 Pharma Vision's participation in Roche accounted for 98.1 percent of its portfolio with the remaining interest of 1.9 percent in Glaxo Wellcome.
